Current dashboard has split server and client build
claim: The current dashboard is packaged as a CLI plus a Hono Node runtime and a separately built Vite React client, with package scripts and bin entries coordinating those pieces.
evidence: package.json declares @hono/node-server, hono, chokidar, @vitejs/plugin-react, vite, dashboard:build, and cartographer-dashboard bin entries.
relevance: TanStack Start should simplify this into one full-stack app surface without breaking the installed CLI contract.

title: Read-only API routes are centralized in Hono app
claim: The current dashboard app registers only GET read-only routes for health, overview, topics, documents, graph, evidence, files, ADRs, index, and events.
evidence: READ_ONLY_ROUTES in dashboard/src/server/dashboard-api.ts lists GET endpoints including /api/events and /api/events/status.
relevance: TanStack Start migration should preserve endpoint semantics or provide compatible route replacements.

title: Chokidar currently drives SSE live reload
claim: The current live reload service watches .plan with Chokidar, ignores .plan/_private, debounces all file events, and publishes LiveReloadEvent records over SSE routes.
evidence: dashboard/src/server/live-reload.ts imports chokidar, configures chokidar.watch(planDir), filters private paths, and registers /api/events plus /api/events/status.
relevance: The requested TanStack DB realtime layer should consume this existing Chokidar event stream rather than inventing another watcher.

title: Client state is currently manual React state plus refetch
claim: DashboardShell currently stores overview, selected topic, ADRs, load errors, and active section in React state and refetches overview/topic/ADR data when live reload events affect visible resources.
evidence: dashboard/src/App.tsx defines useState fields and an effect that calls dashboardApi.overview(), dashboardApi.adrs(), and dashboardApi.topic() after createLiveRefetchPlan.
relevance: This is the state management surface TanStack DB live queries should replace or significantly simplify.

title: Live reload event shape is already shared
claim: LiveReloadEvent and LiveReloadStatus are shared TypeScript models with resource, topic, path, event, changedAt, and watcher-state fields.
evidence: dashboard/src/shared/models.ts defines LiveReloadEvent and LiveReloadStatus used by both server and client code.
relevance: These models are a natural schema seed for TanStack DB collections and realtime event processing.

title: TanStack Start supports colocated server routes
claim: TanStack Start server routes can define HTTP handlers inside createFileRoute route files, allowing client components and server handlers to live in the same full-stack file route system.
evidence: TanStack Start docs show createFileRoute('/hello') with a server.handlers.POST handler and a React component in routes/hello.tsx.
relevance: This directly addresses the user desire to stop managing a separate frontend and server codebase.

title: TanStack Start uses Vite plugin ordering
claim: TanStack Start is configured through @tanstack/react-start/plugin/vite, and the React Vite plugin must come after the Start plugin.
evidence: TanStack Start build-from-scratch docs show plugins: [tanstackStart(), viteReact()] with the note that React's plugin must come after Start's plugin.
relevance: The existing dashboard/vite.config.ts should be replaced or reworked carefully rather than merely adding another plugin anywhere.

title: TanStack DB offers collections and live queries
claim: TanStack DB provides typed collections and React live queries so components can subscribe to filtered, joined, and ordered local data instead of spreading derived state through components.
evidence: TanStack DB docs show createCollection and useLiveQuery over collection data, with automatic updates as data changes.
relevance: This matches the requested realtime state management layer for planning dashboard state.

title: TanStack DB can load collections through TanStack Query
claim: TanStack DB queryCollectionOptions can load collection data through queryKey/queryFn/getKey and supports mutation handlers for API synchronization where needed.
evidence: TanStack DB quick-start docs show createCollection(queryCollectionOptions({ queryKey, queryFn, getKey, onUpdate })) and live queries consuming that collection.
relevance: Existing read-only dashboard API fetches can become query-backed collections before any deeper server route reshaping.

title: Chokidar supports all events and cleanup
claim: Chokidar can watch directories, emit add/change/unlink/addDir/unlinkDir/all/ready/error events, apply ignored callbacks, use ignoreInitial and awaitWriteFinish options, and close watchers asynchronously.
evidence: Chokidar README documents .on('all'), ignored callbacks, ignoreInitial, awaitWriteFinish, and await watcher.close().
relevance: The existing watcher can remain the filesystem boundary while TanStack DB manages client state updates.

title: ADR-0003 currently locks in Hono/Vite dashboard stack
claim: ADR-0003 accepted a local read-only dashboard stack using Hono on Node.js, Chokidar live reload, top-level dashboard/server and dashboard layout, React/Tailwind/shadcn, React Flow, Shiki, and browser/smoke tests.
evidence: ADR-0003 decision and context sections describe the current stack and how future dashboard work should preserve safety boundaries unless explicitly redesigned.
relevance: A TanStack Start conversion is architecture-significant and should produce a new ADR or supersede/amend ADR-0003 after validation.

title: Dashboard must stay local read-only and private-safe
claim: The dashboard contract is a local loopback-only read-only browser view that never writes planning artifacts or source files and excludes raw .plan/_private paths.
evidence: README planning dashboard section states read-only behavior, loopback host rejection, safe .plan live reload, and private raw evidence exclusion.
relevance: TanStack Start and TanStack DB must not expand scope into a writable editor or hosted service.

title: Dashboard tests already cover live reload and privacy boundaries
claim: Existing dashboard tests use fixture roots to verify /api/events status/stream behavior, Chokidar topic changes, read-only routes, and private path blocking.
evidence: tests/dashboard/live-reload.test.ts starts a fixture-root live reload service and tests /api/events; privacy-regressions tests assert READ_ONLY_ROUTES are GET and private files are blocked.
relevance: Migration validation should adapt these tests around TanStack Start routes and TanStack DB update behavior, still using temporary roots.

title: Tests must avoid mutating real planning artifacts
claim: Project instructions require tests and validation fixtures to use temporary/mock project roots rather than the repository's real .plan directory for generated planning artifacts.
evidence: AGENTS.md states tests must never write to the real .plan directory and should scaffold mock projects under /tmp or tempfile.
relevance: TanStack Start route and watcher tests must preserve existing fixture discipline.

title: TanStack packages are not currently declared
claim: Current package metadata does not declare @tanstack/react-start, @tanstack/react-router, @tanstack/react-db, @tanstack/query-db-collection, or @tanstack/react-query.
evidence: Focused repository search for those package names in package.json, package-lock.json, dashboard, and tests returned no matches.
relevance: The migration will require dependency and lockfile changes plus package/script review.
